The periphrastic copula with its English subject is realized by the auxiliary *had*, the only word answering to it.

variant_decisions.evidence: The readings differ only in the order of pronoun and verb; ASV 'when he knew that he was a Roman' renders either.

alignments.note: Rule 21: the dative article takes *the* with the case preposition *on* riding along, headed on *the* under rule 17.

The nominalizing article of the embedded question has no English realization (rules 23 and 61).

Rule 106: the particle *together* realizes the preverb συν- and rides inside the verb's unit, with the infinitival marker as a rule 7 helper; headed on the verb word *come*.

variant_decisions.evidence: ὑπό and παρά with the genitive both mark the agent after a passive; ASV 'he was accused of the Jews' renders either.
ASV reads simply 'he loosed him' with nothing answering ἀπὸ τῶν δεσμῶν ('from his bands'), so the base reading without the phrase is the one rendered.
ASV 'commanded ... all the council to come together' renders the compound συνελθεῖn's 'together', which the simple ἐλθεῖν ('to come') would not supply.
πᾶν and ὅλον are both rendered 'all' before 'the council'; the English does not distinguish them.
ASV reads 'all the council', not 'their council'; the possessive αὐτῶν of the RP reading has no exponent in the English.
